We map out the topological phase diagram based on effective single-band models with and without spin, and use input parameters based on a self-consistent Schrödinger-Poisson calculation of a planar germanium hole gas. As a concrete model for inducing magnetization in the hole gas, we consider the exchange interaction coming from the presence of a dilute ensemble of manganese impurities. A topological phase with $C=3$ could be accessible experimentally in unstrained planar germanium.

title: Mirror symmetry of $\mathcal{N}=(0,4)$ boundary conditions with Nahm poles
summary: We propose mirror symmetry between $\mathcal{N}=(0,4)$ boundary conditions with Nahm poles and Neumann boundary conditions with boundary Fermi multiplets in 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ non-Abelian gauge theories, including $U(N)$ SQCD, $T[SU(N)]$ and the ADHM theories. We obtain the half-indices of the Nahm pole boundary conditions from those of the Dirichlet boundary conditions by Higgsing, where the boundary fugacities are specialized along the principal embedding of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. We check that they agree with the half-indices of the dual Neumann boundary conditions. In the twist limits they give closed-form formulas for the vacuum characters of the boundary vertex operator algebras of Costello and Gaiotto. We find that the unflavored vacuum characters are eta-quotients times quasimodular forms, which we write explicitly in terms of Eisenstein series for all our examples.

title: Multimessenger Exoplanets: Combining Infrared Excess and Astrometry with Gravitational-wave Detections of Double White Dwarf Exoplanets
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Published by The Astrophysical Journal
summary: Multimessenger astrophysics provides a powerful framework for characterizing astrophysical systems through multiple, independent signals rather than relying solely on electromagnetic (EM) observations. While most prior multimessenger studies have focused on the properties of ultracompact objects, recent work has shown that gravitational waves (GWs) detectable with the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) observatory can also be used to detect exoplanets orbiting stellar remnants. In particular, this includes circumbinary planets around tight double white dwarf (DWD) systems. This population is unique: no such planets are currently known around DWDs, and only a handful of circumbinary planets around main-sequence stars and planets orbiting white dwarfs (WDs) have been identified. Independent EM confirmation will be essential, especially for the first GW-detected exoplanets, to validate this method. While EM techniques are unlikely to efficiently survey large populations of DWDs, GW detection followed by targeted EM confirmation provides one pathway for identifying and characterizing these systems. Using a representative case, the known DWD ZTF J2243+5242 scaled to a fiducial distance of 150 pc, we compute the detectability of circumbinary exoplanets via LISA GW observations. We then demonstrate two complementary EM techniques--JWST infrared (IR) excess and Gaia or Habitable Worlds Observatory astrometry--that could independently confirm a GW-detected planet in this fiducial system. We present the first exploration of IR excess around DWDs as a viable exoplanet detection method, extending its established use for solitary WDs. Both EM techniques overlap with regions of parameter space where LISA is sensitive to DWD exoplanets, enabling robust confirmation and characterization.

title: Construction and Commissioning of the Warwick TPC Platform
summary: Active-target gas time projection chambers (TPCs) could provide the ultimate measurements of neutrino interactions needed for future neutrino oscillation measurements. Their development requires optimisation of the gas mixture, pressure, electric fields, and readout configuration. Warwick TPC (WarTPC) is an R\&D platform for investigating in these directions for neutrino physics and beyond. It can operate at pressures up to approximately 10 bar and features a combination of thick gas electron multipliers and a Timepix3 camera for optical readout. In this paper, we present the construction and commissioning of the WarTPC platform, describing the design and integration of its subsystems, and report the first measurements of its optical response under different operating conditions, demonstrating a stable and functioning R&D platform.

title: Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations
summary: Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.

title: Selective coupling and spectral evolution of topological domain-wall states under local perturbations
summary: In this work we investigate the spectral evolution of topological domain-wall states in a one-dimensional structure described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model. We show that a local potential applied to the domain wall induces a selective coupling between a topological state and specific bulk states. Moreover, by increasing the gate potential, we observe that the domain wall state energies asymptotically reach a bulk band, whereas new domain wall states appear on the opposite side of the band. As a consequence, the domain-wall-state spectrum evolves through a sequence of localized states that remain separated from the bulk continuum. These effects are also reflected in transport calculations, where the conductance peaks follow the evolution of the energy spectrum. To experimentally verify these phenomena, we realize an RLC topo-electrical circuit and perform impedance spectroscopy measurements. We find that the impedance matches the local density of states, exhibiting resonances at frequencies associated with the bulk energies that selectively couple to the domain wall topological state.

title: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
summary: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.

title: Linear monitoring-feedback Model for Linearized gravity
summary: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics. Auxiliary systems monitor the positions of massive bodies, and their records are fed back through a chosen gravitational response kernel. At the level of linear input-output theory, this construction makes the deterministic response explicit while exposing the force noise and correlations associated with the auxiliary sector. We organize the allowed ancilla correlations into three regimes. In Regime-I, independent ancillas have unsqueezed, uncorrelated sensing and back-action quadratures. A single object then has a minimum classical-gravity noise (CGN), S_F^min = 2 hbar M Omega_SN^2, where Omega_SN is the Schrodinger-Newton frequency set by the microscopic mass distribution. In Regime-II, arbitrary local sensing--back-action correlations are allowed, but the ancillas associated with different objects remain independent. The single-object CGN is then unrestricted, while the joint force-noise matrix obeys a determinant bound that is equivalent to the local classical-channel/no-entanglement bound. In Regime-III, cross-object correlations and a common nonlocal mediator are allowed. The commuting force noises can then be jointly squeezed, entanglement between the masses can occur, and--with a suitable retarded response and input state--the monitoring-feedback system can reproduce the noise and commutators of linearized quantum gravity, including non-Markovian quantum fluctuations.

title: Many-body Response to Spin-Independent and Spin-Dependent Dark Matter Scattering in a Superfluid Helium-3 Target
summary: The QUEST-DMC experiment employs an ultra-low-temperature superfluid $^3$He target in an effort to detect sub-GeV dark matter (DM). The low-momentum scattering of such light DM is sensitive to the many-body structure of superfluid $^3$He, making it necessary to account for the collective behaviour of the medium. We present a first-principles calculation of the DM scattering rate in this inherently quantum many-body medium for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions. The leading consequence of this many-body behaviour is a kinematic enhancement of the scattering rate arising from the Fermi-Dirac statistics of the ultra-low-temperature target. Accounting for this extends the projected reach to lower DM masses for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions under the benchmark detector assumptions considered here. The resulting sensitivity improvement becomes increasingly pronounced as the detector threshold drops into the sub-eV regime. It is negligible at the conventional readout threshold of approximately $31$ eV, but becomes significant at the $0.51$ eV benchmark threshold for SQUID-based readout. Specifically, at this threshold, incorporating the many-body response extends the higher-energy recoil tail and improves the projected low-mass reach by approximately $2.5\%$ relative to the single-atom approximation. This improvement becomes more pronounced at lower thresholds. Reaching a threshold of $5$ meV could further extend the sensitivity of QUEST-DMC into the realm of sub-MeV DM.

title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
summary: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schrödinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

title: Data-driven exploration of the strength-ductility synergy in refractory high-entropy alloys
summary: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) have attracted increasing attention for their exceptional ability to retain strength at high temperatures. However, current research mainly concentrates on compositions close to equimolar alloys, leaving a large part of the composition space unexplored. Here, we develop a multiscale framework based on a data-driven dislocation genome method that constructs energy landscapes for edge dislocation motion across various compositions. The local configurational force derived from the energy landscape is incorporated into dislocation dynamics simulations, revealing a scaling law connecting macroscale strength and atomic-scale local resistance governed by fluctuations in the local configurational force. Based on this scaling law, a new solid-solution strengthening model for edge dislocation in BCC alloys is developed, followed by a data-driven exploration of refractory alloys considering both strength and ductility. The developed method and theory are adaptable, allowing for extension to other BCC alloy systems and guiding high-throughput alloy design.

title: Destabilization of Abelian-Higgs vortices at large Chern-Simons coupling
summary: We study the effect of the Chern--Simons (CS) coupling on the radial spectral stability of axially symmetric vortices in the $(2+1)$-dimensional Abelian--Higgs model. From the linear stability approach, we obtain the dispersion relations of gauge field perturbations, which signal the existence of a critical CS coupling $k_{\rm c}$ that depends on Maxwell's coupling constant. For $k<k_{\rm c}$, the continuous spectrum is purely imaginary and the modes remain gapped. At $k=k_{\rm c}$, one of the modes becomes gapless, while for $k>k_{\rm c}$ real eigenvalues appear, corresponding to exponentially growing radial modes. Direct time-evolution simulations are consistent with the spectral analysis, which shows instability for $k>k_{\rm c}$. Below the threshold, the perturbed vortex relaxes toward its stationary profile, whereas above the threshold, growing fluctuations deform the core and propagate outward. These results show that the CS coupling controls radial spectral stability of Abelian-Higgs vortices, and destabilization occurs for sufficiently large CS coupling, relative to the Maxwell coupling.

title: Axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant: Bayesian constraints from current cosmological data
summary: We constrain canonical axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant using DES Year 5 supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, compressed CMB information, and geometry-corrected Gold-2017 growth data. We solve the background and linear-growth equations and sample with PolyChord. Our joint prior is logarithmic in the decay constant over $0.005\leq f/M_{\rm Pl}\leq10$ and uniform in the initial angle $θ_i=φ_i/f\in[0,π]$, conditioned on $π-θ_i\geq H_{\rm inf}/(2πf)$ with $H_{\rm inf}=10^{13}$ GeV and reduced Planck mass $M_{\rm Pl}$. The broad-prior model favors recent thawing, with median $w_{{\rm DE},0}=-0.865^{+0.068}_{-0.053}$, $m_φ\in[0.91,4.39]\times10^{-33}$ eV, and $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.589,4.899]$ (central 68\% credible intervals). Bayes factors relative to flat $Λ$CDM are 0.70 and 30.1 for the normalized fluctuation-conditioned prior (Convention I) and its further conditioning on numerical acceptance (Convention II). Restricting $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$ gives $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.262,0.822]$ at 68\% credibility and Bayes factors 0.233 and 32.4. Relative to the zero-vacuum axion model, the broad-prior Bayes factors are 0.620 and 1.65, providing no compelling evidence for a negative cosmological constant. Local likelihood optimization gives an Akaike information criterion difference $Δ{\rm AIC}\simeq-10.87$ for the zero-vacuum model relative to flat $Λ$CDM. For this model, assuming that the instanton generating $m_φ^2f^2=Λ_{\rm UV}^4e^{-S_{\rm inst}}$ satisfies the axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture, the one-sided 95\% posterior lower limit on the minimum compatible coefficient $c_{\min}$ rises from 37 to 55 as the ultraviolet scale $Λ_{\rm UV}$ increases from $10^{-10}M_{\rm Pl}$ to $M_{\rm Pl}$, in tension with an order-one coefficient under these assumptions.

title: Quantum tomography of Higgsstrahlung: Higgs boson self-coupling and $Z$ boson anomalous couplings
summary:
The Higgs boson self-coupling enters the Higgsstrahlung process $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at one loop. The three diagrams that carry it project onto two Lorentz structures: the tree-level one, which rescales the rate, and that of the CP-even anomalous coupling $b_Z$, which changes the polarization of the final-state $Z$ boson.
  To assess how well quantum state tomography constrains the $hZZ$ anomalous couplings and the trilinear coupling at FCC-ee, we compute the helicity density matrix of the $Z$ boson, for an effective vertex that also includes a CP-odd anomalous coupling $\tilde b_Z$, together with its complete one-loop correction in the Standard Model. With these corrections and no other new physics in the effective vertex, quantum state tomography determines $κ_λ$ to $\pm 3.9$, or $\pm 2.9$ with the full angular information, independently of the rate and of the normalization of the vertex, and not far from the limit $δκ_λ\simeq 1$ set by the quantum Fisher information. Without assumptions on the new physics, quantum tomography directly bounds the anomalous couplings at the $10^{-3}$ level, improving on the existing projections.
  The density matrix also characterizes the $Z$ boson as a qutrit. At $365$ GeV its state in the central region is pure enough to violate the Klyachko--Can--Binicioğlu--Shumovsky contextuality inequality, $\mathbb{CNTXT}_5 = 2.06$ at $θ= π/2$ against the non-contextual bound $2$. We also quantify the purity and the amount of magic of the $Z$ boson state, using the mana, the stabilizer Rényi entropy and the robustness of magic for the latter. At fixed angle, purity, contextuality and magic are robust against anomalous couplings of the size probed by the tomography. The inclusive state, instead, is neither contextual in this test nor magic in the helicity basis.

title: All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model
summary: In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=λΔ+\tanπ(θ+n^2α)δ_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $λ>0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(α, θ)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} 49(8), 509--512 (1982)] in the study of the quantum suppression of chaos: The pseudo-randomness of the sequence $\{\tanπ(θ+n^2α)\}_{n\in\Bbb Z}$ (for $α\in\Bbb T\setminus \Bbb Q$) should result in all coupling Anderson localization for $H$ similar to that for the one-dimensional Anderson model. Our proof is based on nonperturbative Green's function estimates approach using Cayley transform, quadratic Weyl sum estimate and Rellich function analysis.

title: Unified constitutive model of body-centered cubic metals informed by discrete dislocation dynamics
summary: Predicting plastic flow in body-centered cubic metals across temperature and strain-rate regimes requires distinguishing structural resistance from kinetic contributions. Here, we develop a temperature dependent mobility law for screw dislocation, integrating thermal activation theory and relativistic effects. Through discrete dislocation dynamics simulations, uniaxial tension and compression simulations were conducted on configurations with different initial dislocation densities, elucidating the correlation between plastic strain rate and key parameters such as stress, temperature, and dislocation density. Subsequently, a unified constitutive model incorporating temperature and strain rate is derived based on microscopic mechanisms. The model naturally bridges microscopic mechanisms to continuum response, resolving the additivity dilemma by establishing explicit physical criteria for how structural resistances and competing kinetic mechanisms superimpose. Through rigorous bottom-up simulations, we quantitatively capture the crossover point where phonon drag overtakes thermal activation, providing a mechanism-based explanation of anomalous thermal hardening. This work enables physically consistent predictions of strength and creep behavior across broad temperature and strain-rate regimes, advancing beyond phenomenological descriptions toward transparent, mechanism-based alloy design.

title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
summary: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

title: General $δN$ formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory
summary: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the $δN$ formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.

title: Towards an improved understanding of $a_1$ and $a_2$ transition form factors
summary: The isovector axial-vector and tensor meson states $a_1$ and $a_2$ have garnered interest in the last years since they appear as intermediate states in the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution to $(g-2)_μ$. Their dynamical behaviour including their transition form factors is poorly understood to this day, which also affects the uncertainty budget of the HLbL contribution. In order to improve the situation, we construct the $a_1$ and $a_2$ as resonances in the $ρπ$ system, which allows us to express the relevant amplitudes in terms of known form factors and properties of the resonances. With this, we aim to obtain a phenomenologically well motivated parameterisation of the transition form factors built from the general principles of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry.

title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
summary: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.

title: Machine-learning charge density for electronic materials and devices simulation
summary: We present a machine-learning (ML) charge density model, DeltaChargeNet, integrated with the full-potential tight-binding muffin-tin orbital (FP-TB-MTO) method for electronic structure and quantum transport simulations of materials and devices. The ML model predicts electron density from atomic structures with low linear-scaling cost, while FP-TB-MTO provides an accurate tight-binding representation of the system Hamiltonian. To achieve high-fidelity ML density for complex devices with interfaces and disorder, we train an equivariant graph convolutional network to predict $Δρ$-the difference between DFT and atomic superposition densities-under a charge neutrality constraint required for inhomogeneous systems. A secondary ML residual charge model compensates for errors in the primary $Δρ$ model. The predicted density is then used within the full-relativistic FP-TB-MTO framework combined with the non-equilibrium Green's function method. We validate our method on bulk HgCdTe disordered alloys (including vacancy defects) and Au/HgCdTe/Au disordered devices. The maximum band energy error is below 10 meV for bulk HgCdTe. For devices, the charge neutrality constraint suppresses long-wavelength charge bias that would otherwise distort the electrostatic potential by 0.68-1.88 eV near the device center, while residual compensation corrects the remaining 0.16-0.46 eV potential mismatch, essential for reproducing the correct potential barrier profile. Together, these corrections reproduce the layer-resolved potential, including interface steps and bulk-like plateaus, within 0.1 eV of fully self-consistent DFT. Finally, we demonstrate quantum transport in a 11220-atom infrared detector. By combining first-principles accuracy with linear-scaling inference, DeltaChargeNet enables large-scale device simulations without the full DFT self-consistent field loop.

title: Gravitational Corrections to OPE Coefficients
summary: The short-distance singular behavior of correlation functions of quantum field theories in curved spacetime is a universal property shared by all well-behaved states (known as Hadamard states). For two-point functions this takes the form of the Hadamard tail of free scalars and its generalizations to spinning fields and interacting theories. In this work, we compute similar universal curvature corrections to curved-space OPE coefficients in a short-distance expansion for interacting quantum field theories in general dimensions. We work at leading order in the curvature but for arbitrary backgrounds. Examples include weakly coupled scalar field theories with cubic and quartic interactions as well as strongly coupled conformal field theories. The gravitationally dressed OPE coefficients allow us to test explicitly, and confirm, the validity of the smearing-in-time procedure discussed by Witten in the construction of the algebra of observables near an observer's worldline in curved spacetime.

title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
comment: 63 pages, 1 table, 5 figures. Ready for submission to Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics (JCAP)
summary: Recent observational investigation of cosmological Parity Violation (PV) through the galaxy Four-point Correlation Function (4PCF) has motivated a careful theoretical examination of potential systematic contributions. In this work, we demonstrate that parity-odd contributions to the isotropic 4PCF estimator induced by Redshift Space Distortion (RSD), up to the leading order $\mathcal{H}/k$ of general relativistic corrections, vanish upon averaging over all the Line-of-Sight (LOS). We analyse the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density, combining the biased tracer expansion and the dark matter gravitational dynamics within the framework of Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory (EPT) to third order in the density perturbation. Building on prior studies of the parity-odd mode of the trispectrum (the Fourier-space counterpart of the 4PCF), we extend existing results in three directions: incorporating the wide-angle effect by adopting a local LOS definition for each galaxy in the 4PCF, accounting for tidal bias in the galaxy population, and generalising the assessment to an arbitrary cosmological background. Expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, we show that angular momentum selection rules, encoded in the Wigner 3-j symbols, enforce that only parity-even contributions survive the integration over all LOS orientations, both in the plane-parallel approximation and in the full wide-angle case. This result is crucial for large-scale statistical analyses using isotropic estimators. It supports interpreting possible PV detections as a signal not due to a systematic RSD artefact. We conclude with a discussion of the caveats of our results and identify potential sources of PV.

title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
summary: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $Ω(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

title: A Unified Device-Level Physical Framework for DRAM Read Disturbance
summary: Read disturbance in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) depends on both local device interactions and the electrical conditions imposed by shared array circuitry. Here, we combine DIMM-level characterization results, device measurements, and TCAD simulations to interpret RowHammer, RowPress, and ColumnDisturb within a unified device-level physical framework. We relate charge evolution at the floating storage node to three key mechanisms: trap-assisted electron migration (EM), capacitive coupling (CC), and sense-amplifier-mediated disturb (SAMD). EM is local and trap-sensitive, while CC weakens with wordline separation. SAMD extends disturbance through shared column circuitry by modifying unselected-cell leakage under rail-level bitline biases, a contribution supported by the approximately ninefold higher OFF-state leakage measured relative to retention-like conditions for a high-voltage storage state. These distinct spatial ranges account for localized RowHammer and RowPress failures and remote ColumnDisturb populations with abrupt changes at subarray boundaries. We further interpret prolonged RowPress activation as a transition from an initial RowHammer-like transient to sustained leakage driven mainly by SAMD under held wordline and bitline biases. Within this device-level framework, trap effectiveness and storage-state-dependent leakage provide an interpretation of previously puzzling failure signatures, including the earlier onset of 0-to-1 RowHammer failures despite the predominance of 1-to-0 failures at high hammer counts. The same framework explains the observed RowPress and ColumnDisturb polarities and the duration-dependent reversal of neighboring- and passing-wordline effectiveness. These results provide a physical basis for developing compact DRAM reliability models across access patterns and array configurations.

title: Exploring M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$: Mellin amplitudes with composite operators
summary: We bootstrap mixed correlators in M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$, focusing on tree-level correlation functions involving one double-particle operator and three single-particle operators. Combining inputs from AdS/CFT, the chiral algebra, and the OPE at large central charge, we uniquely determine the Mellin amplitude for $\langle [{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{q}]{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{p}{\cal O}_{p+q-2}\rangle$ for generic $p$ and $q$. While our main focus is the $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ SCFT in six dimensions, we also derive the analogous result in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, applying the same bootstrap approach to $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM. Despite their different dynamics, the resulting Mellin amplitudes exhibit a strikingly similar structure, with non-trivial OPE predictions for low-twist protected operators providing a key input. Our work is motivated by recent developments in the study of Kaluza-Klein correlators in bubbling geometries, where four-point functions involving single- and multi-particle operators are computed as response functions to smooth deformations of the vacuum geometry. While well tested in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, we aim to extend this framework to M-theory.

title: Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?
summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in dynamical dark energy, and naturally raise the question of whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics. We address this question through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark-energy contribution to the expansion and the gravitational responses governing clustering and lensing, complemented by a combined covariance-mode analysis, without imposing model-specific relations between the sectors. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernova observations, and subsequently adding large scale structure observations including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data and other surveys, we recover a broad maximum in the effective dark-energy density near $z\simeq0.6$--$0.7$. The gravitational responses exhibit suggestive low-redshift enhancements over their GR values, approximately coincident with the background feature. Adding large scale structure information preserves the background feature but favours a mildly reduced lensing response. The combined covariance-mode analysis identifies the combinations of background and gravitational responses most tightly constrained by current observations and quantifies their departures from $Λ$CDM. The leading modes are decisively background dominated, while the gravitational sector remains less precisely constrained. Thus, present data cannot yet determine whether the suggestive low-redshift features in the two sectors share a common physical origin, a question that ongoing Stage-IV surveys will be able to address

title: Methanol substitution suppresses deflagration-excited knock and increases the efficiency of a hydrogen-fuelled CFR engine
summary: Knock restricts the performance of hydrogen spark-ignition engines and is usually attributed to end-gas autoignition. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first study in which methanol is used to replace part of the hydrogen in a hydrogen engine at constant fuel energy addition, and it shows that near the knock boundary the limiting oscillation is excited by the deflagration itself, which methanol removes without derating the performance. Port-injected methanol replaced 20--50% of the hydrogen energy in a variable-compression Cooperative Fuel Research engine at 600 rpm and compression ratios of 8--12. With pure hydrogen, oscillation in the 4--15 kHz range began before 10% of the charge had burned in 97--100% of cycles, and its maximum amplitude (MAPO) followed the maximum pressure-rise rate across 2499 cycles (Spearman $ρ=0.94$). Methanol slowed the deflagration: it replaced high-flame-speed hydrogen, cooled the intake by 24--25 K and, at unchanged intake pressure, enleaned the mixture by 10--13%. At 50% methanol, the 10--90% combustion duration lengthened 2.7--3.0-fold, oscillation onset moved 4.5--8.3$^\circ$CA after CA10 and mean MAPO fell by 89--93% although the spark timing was advanced by 13--19$^\circ$CA, and IMEP and indicated thermal efficiency rose by 2.4--7.8%. Methanol was thus worth more than this advance, and at matched CA50 MAPO was still about 90% lower. The measured combustion duration of all 25 data sets scaled with the computed laminar flame speed as $S_L^{-0.58}$ ($R^2=0.99$); fuel replacement accounted for about three quarters of the reduction in $S_L$, and the end-gas autoignition integral stayed below 0.07, against 1 at autoignition. The chamber kept its cylindrical acoustic modes, whose frequencies fell by 8--9%. The trade-off is formaldehyde emissions, which rose five- to sixfold while NO$_x$ fell by 49--85%.

title: Quantum spin-wave statistics and dimensionality in thermally activated magnetic transitions
summary: A quantum correction to the rate of thermally activated transition between magnetic states is formulated within harmonic transition state theory and the Kramers-Langer theory by employing quantum statistics for stable spin-wave excitations around the initial state and the transition state. Quantum spin-wave statistics modifies both parameters of the Arrhenius expression for the transition rate relative to their classical values: the zero-point fluctuations renormalize the energy barrier, while the Bose-Einstein occupation of the spin-wave modes modifies the pre-exponential factor. Comparison of the classical and quantum-statistical pre-exponential factors reveals a systematic error associated with the excessive weight assigned to high-frequency excitations by classical equipartition. This error accumulates over the spin-wave spectrum and becomes increasingly severe with increasing dimensionality of the system. The effect is demonstrated for coherent magnetization reversal, and transitions involving noncollinear magnetic textures, including collapse of a magnetic skyrmion and rupture of a skyrmion tube, where classical and quantum-statistical predictions for the transition rate can differ by many orders of magnitude in three-dimensional systems.

title: The Spectral Anatomy of Complex-Time Singularities
summary: The properties of the bulk spacetime in a holographic theory may be probed by the analytic structure of the boundary correlator $G(t,x)$. In this letter, we analyse the singularities of $G(t,x)$ by deriving them from Fourier space. We show that the quasinormal modes are characterised by two distinct momentum scaling regimes. The first regime is defined by a finite $k/ω^γ$ for some characteristic exponent $γ$ which is extracted from the singularity, and probes $G(t,0)$, reproducing the bouncing geodesic analysis. The second regime is defined by a finite $k/ω$, and probes the complexified bulk away from the singularity, which allows us to study the singularities of $G(t,x\neq 0)$. We extract coefficients and exponents of the singularities for general spacetime dimensions, and allow for more exotic interiors. The heavy reliance of our computation on quasinormal modes opens the doors to a similar analysis being done on spacetimes that are accessible only numerically.

title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in non-standard late-time evolution. We investigate whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density, $Ω_{\rm X}(a)$, and the gravitational response functions $μ(a)$ and $Σ(a)$. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, and large scale structure observations, including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data, we perform reconstructions with and without a theory motivated correlation prior derived from stable Horndeski models. We find a persistent maximum in $Ω_{\rm X}$ at $z\simeq0.5$--$0.7$, corresponding to a crossing of the effective phantom divide. This feature is already present in the CMB+BAO combination and remains robust when modifications to clustering and lensing are allowed. The reconstructed gravitational response exhibits suggestive enhancements in $μ$ and $Σ$ over approximately the same redshift range, although these departures are less significant. Including LSS information instead favours a reduced lensing response, $Σ<1$, while leaving the background feature largely unchanged. An interpretation within Generalized Brans-Dicke theories illustrates how modifications to the effective gravitational coupling and a scalar-mediated fifth force may contribute to these trends. Our results indicate that current departures from $Λ$CDM are most significant in the expansion history, while leaving open the possibility of correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics that future Stage IV surveys can test.

title: Quantum Fundamental Groups of Spaces with Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
summary: Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology. We characterize quantum fundamental groups for a wide class of examples, including $\mathbb{RP}^2$. We show that these quantum fundamental groups are genuinely quantum for spaces with finite fundamental groups that are either non-abelian or of non prime order.

title: Stress peaks and rupture in star-polymer networks with bidisperse arm lengths
summary: The tensile response of phantom star-polymer networks with bidisperse arm lengths is examined by energy-minimization simulations. Short and long precursors form short-short, short-long, and long-long strands within one end-linked network. The contrast among these strands, composition, functionality, and reaction conversion are varied, and their effects on network rupture are examined. At a large length contrast, two stress peaks appear over part of the composition range. In such realizations, short-short strands carry most of the stress at the first peak, while short-long strands carry most of it after the intervening stress drop. Interesting findings are i) that the peak stretches, including those in double-peak cases, follow composition-dependent master curves when plotted against cycle-rank density, as in monodisperse networks, and ii) that a recently proposed mechanical model describes their cycle-rank dependence, with parameters that vary with composition and arm-length contrast. The parameters differ between the peak series, although their separate determination is limited in some conditions. In addition, the Mark-type improvement of the mechanical properties of the networks by adding a fraction of short strands is discussed. With the implemented FENE force law, the work up to the global stress peak is closer to the long-only value, but an improvement above that reference is not statistically resolved.

title: Geometric Quantization of the Giant Graviton Master Moduli Space
summary: We describe a remarkable reorganization of the space of gauge invariant operators of free or twisted $U(N)$ gauge theories as combinations of single-trace and determinant operators modulo certain "open loop equations". The reorganization has a transparent holographic interpretation, describing how states at finite $N$ can be reproduced by imposing certain $N$-independent gauge constraints on the combination of the closed strings Fock space and a geometric quantization of the moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes, with quantization parameter $N^{-1}$. The moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes is reproduced from tachyon condensation of auxiliary D-brane/anti-D-brane pairs which are "Koszul dual" to the D-brane system which supports the original gauge theory. We describe how to impose the open loop equations via certain BRST complexes and conjecture that their homology recovers the finite $N$ BPS Hilbert space in the limit of large auxiliary rank. The BRST construction conjecturally categorifies Murthy's Giant Graviton Expansion of indices counting $U(N)$-invariant BPS operators.

title: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $Γ$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
summary:
We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $Γ$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile.
  The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.

title: Foundation Tensor Networks Generalize Across Quantum Lattice Systems
summary: Neural quantum states and tensor networks have emerged as leading techniques for simulating quantum many-body systems. However, disordered systems remain extremely challenging in both frameworks as they require computation of the ground state for every realization of the disorder. Recently, neural quantum states have been used to construct foundation models that generate the ground state directly from the Hamiltonian. Still, they are hindered by the need to perform extensive sampling to estimate observables. To address these difficulties, we introduce the foundation tensor network (FTN), which uses a neural network to generate the tensor network representation of the ground-state wavefunction from the Hamiltonian. To accelerate training, we develop a technique, called \texttt{GridBP}, based on iterated one-dimensional belief propagation that reduces the cost of computing the energy expectation value to just two tensor contractions. We use FTNs to calculate the critical parameters of the glass transition in the quantum Edwards-Anderson model via finite-size scaling analysis. To facilitate rapid averaging, we use a moment-generating function to evaluate the order parameter, lowering the cost to a single tensor contraction. We obtain high-fidelity estimates for the critical parameters by averaging over 500,000 disorder realizations.

title: From pure spinor modules to superspace superfields
summary: We relate the pure spinor formalism to the superspace description of constrained superfields and gauge multiplets, mainly for abelian two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry, with three- and four-dimensional N=1 examples for comparison. For each multiplet we give an explicit module over the supertranslation Chevalley-Eilenberg algebra and match its reconstruction with the known superfields. First-order constraints come from modules supported on linear subspaces of the nilpotence variety, and higher-order ones, such as the complex-linear constraint, from Yoneda products of their Ext classes. Requiring a connection to act on given matter and its conjugate restricts its curvature, which yields the ordinary, twisted and semichiral vector multiplets with their field strengths. The module of each vector multiplet is the fiber product over the origin of the coordinate rings of the matter supports: its potentials are differences of partial potentials, and its gauge parameters are the matter superfields. For the large vector multiplet this fiber product is not a quotient of the pure spinor ring; its field strengths are four odd semichiral superfields, and partial regluing gives its constrained versions.

title: Red-Blue Hamiltonian Tomography via the Operator Lightcone Wavemap
summary: We introduce a model-free method for Hamiltonian tomography based on the operator spreading wavefront. Given two tensor network simulations of the same quantum lattice (one with the nominal Hamiltonian and one with one or more perturbed bonds), the signed cross-entropy of the non-identity Pauli weight field $\mathcal{L}(v,t) = -\ln(n_{\rm pert}/n_{\rm base})$ identifies each perturbed bond by its causal signature: a red-blue sign flip at the two endpoints, visible from the first wavefront crossing. Combining measurements from $p$ strategically placed observation centers via an ensemble log-likelihood sum, a single broken bond is identified with an 82-fold margin over the next candidate on a $7\times7$ lattice. Extending to realistic coupling degradation ($δJ = -0.20$) and up to 8 simultaneous faults, the integrated log-ratio $Λ(v) = \ln(\mathcal{B}(v)/\mathcal{N}(v))$ achieves a per-bond detection rate above 90\% in a single seismic pass using only 6 simulations. An iterative re-scan strategy progressively resolves multi-bond cases as the signal clears with each recalibration pass. The method requires no model assumptions and no knowledge of the perturbation type or magnitude; the detection is deliberately blind.

title: Crystal Structure Prediction from Search to Learning: A 30-Year Expedition
summary: Crystal structure prediction (CSP) determines periodic atomic or molecular arrangements from chemical composition and physical conditions. Over three decades, CSP has evolved from chemical construction and global energy optimization to hybrid approaches combining symmetry, learned potentials, adaptive search, and deep generative models. This survey reviews method, software, review, and benchmark records from 1996 to October 2026, covering inorganic and molecular crystals, including formula-conditioned diffusion, flow, and autoregressive models that preserve composition. We classify methods by candidate construction and exploration: template and discrete construction, random search, evolutionary search, swarm and differential evolution, energy-landscape exploration, adaptive machine-learning-guided search, and learned generation. We distinguish representation, relaxation, ranking, and physical qualification. Benchmarks reveal no universally dominant approach. In a 46-target leaderboard snapshot, the best-performing template method achieves higher top-1 recovery than leading generative models, but paired tests show no statistically significant differences from several generative competitors. We also audit predictions for 68 experimentally examined materials, including 52 with structures confirmed by diffraction or microscopy. Predictions for 23 of the 68 preceded experiment, mostly through first-principles global search. Within the reviewed evidence, we find no independently confirmed discovery in which a deep generative model predicted the structure before experiment. We conclude with the principal limitations of current CSP algorithms and priorities for future research.

title: Resurgence without the Borel Plane: Mellin-Barnes Summation and Analytic Stokes Reconstruction
summary:
We develop a route to resurgence without the Borel plane: sums of divergent perturbative series and their encoded nonperturbative monodromy are constructed directly in complex perturbative order. In the Analytic Umbral Framework (AUF), an analytic coefficient clock produces the sum through a Mellin-Barnes integral and its monodromy through a bare inverse Mellin transform. Neither a Borel transform nor continuation of a Borel germ is required for this construction. For Watson-admissible Gevrey clocks, the completion agrees with the canonical Borel-Laplace sum in the guaranteed directions. When the admissible aperture exceeds $2π$, the clockwise difference of adjacent logarithmic determinations is given by $2πi$ times the inverse-Mellin carrier. This carrier is also the AUF completion of a null clock and is flat on the overlap. The sum and its aggregate monodromy are thus obtained ''in one shot'', before resolving individual actions and fluctuation series.
  Euler's equation, zero-dimensional quartic models, the scaled Gamma function and a solvable $O(4)$ toy model exemplify the procedure, and show how further analysis recovers directional Stokes variations. The lognormal benchmark extends the construction beyond every finite Gevrey order: no finite-order Borel transform gives a convergent germ, yet explicit clock-selection conditions yield an AUF completion and a nonzero ordinary flat carrier. Distributed relaxation supplies a physical realization of this growth class. AUF therefore both reconstructs familiar resurgent information without Borel-plane continuation and extends completion beyond finite-order Borel-Laplace summation.

title: Annihilation versus anchoring of a topologically charged pair on a perforated two-dimensional surface
summary: Two independent random walks of opposite topological charge move on the discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$, which contains $k$ well-separated holes. The walks annihilate when they come within a core distance of each other, and each walk is anchored when it first touches a hole. We prove that the probability of annihilation before anchoring converges to $w_0/(w_0+\sum_j w_j)$, where the weights are explicit and depend only logarithmically on the sizes of the core and of the holes; for point-like core and holes, the limit is $1/(1+k)$. We then prove a fate theorem: the pair either terminates or ends as two opposite charges anchored on two different holes, with probability $(k-1)/(k+1)$ in the point-like case, and the hosting pair $\{j,l\}$ is chosen with probability proportional to $w_jw_l$. The proof combines an abstract competition lemma for rare sets in reversible Markov chains with sharp two-dimensional Green's function estimates.

title: Electric Fields Turn Vacancy-trapping Grain Boundaries into Li-Ion Pathways in Li2O
summary: Ion transport in solids has conventionally been understood from equilibrium diffusion, yet ions in batteries are driven by electric fields. Does field-driven ion transport follow equilibrium behavior? We examined this question in bulk Li2O and at its grain boundaries (GBs) using electric-field molecular dynamics combining a machine learning interatomic potential with a Bader charge prediction model. Although Li diffusion in cubic Li2O is isotropic at zero field, an electric field renders it orientation dependent because Li hops along a limited set of crystallographic pathways that the field biases unequally. At GBs, this anisotropy becomes a qualitative difference: a GB that strongly traps Li vacancies but exhibits a strong field response releases them under a field, whereas a weakly responsive GB retains them despite weaker vacancy trapping. These results show that field-driven GB transport is governed not by static thermodynamics alone but by the angle between the electric field and the diffusion pathways of the constituent grains.

title: fieldsmith: Automated symbolic derivation in classical field theory and gauge theory from LaTeX input
summary: We present fieldsmith, an open-source Python library for the automated derivation of analytical results in classical field theory, and non-abelian gauge theories. A Lagrangian is entered the way it is written on a blackboard, in LaTeX index notation, and the library produces and verifies Euler-Lagrange equations (of arbitrary derivative order, on flat or curved backgrounds), Noether currents and identities, canonical and Hilbert energy-momentum tensors, canonical momenta and Hamiltonians, local Poisson brackets and a Dirac-Bergmann constraint analysis with degree-of-freedom counting, linearised wave equations and dispersion relations, gauge-covariant derivatives and field strengths for products of unitary groups, and mass spectra after spontaneous symmetry breaking. A fitting routine translates component-level output back into covariant index notation, and a grading module checks students' submitted field equations, identities and conserved currents. The implementation is a compact (about 2,700 lines) layer on top of SymPy: tensors are stored by components with labelled, variance-aware slots, and every statement is established by exact symbolic computation rather than pattern matching. This document is the companion guide to the library. It explains the intent and design, describes the algorithms, and then works through eighteen self-checking examples, ranging from the Klein-Gordon field to the BPST instanton and the 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole, each preceded by the background physics needed to follow it. The examples double as a compact introduction to classical field theory and gauge theory as seen through a computational lens. We are explicit about the limitations of the approach.

title: Global saddle selection and exact absolute-instability boundaries for convection in porous media with throughflow
summary: In the Darcy-Prats problem, horizontal throughflow leaves the temporal onset of convection unchanged but raises the heating required for a localized disturbance to grow at a fixed point. The saddle equations give five candidates, but only the saddles reached by deformation of the Fourier contour contribute to the growth. For $Ra>π^2$, $Pe>0$ we prove that the same off-axis pair contributes throughout the domain: no Stokes transition can change its contribution. Its growth gives a unique analytic absolute threshold, first reached by the lowest vertical mode. Rescaling transfers the selection to Forchheimer drag, transverse rolls of a power-law fluid, anisotropic permeability, an open upper boundary and a vertical magnetic field. A shift of the same growth function accounts for interphase heat exchange in a model of metallic foam. At prescribed throughflow the threshold increases strictly with either resistance coefficient. In particular, a vertical magnetic field raises the absolute threshold at fixed Péclet number. Tabulated thresholds check the reduction. Algebraic elimination gives the boundary polynomial, and frequency recovery selects its physical branch. At the Darcy level the selected saddles trace an arc of the elliptic curve 11a3, a degeneration of a genus-two family at nonzero shifted levels. Series inversion on this arc gives an integer weak-throughflow series and an all-order strong-throughflow expansion. Rational certificates establish the exact convergence radii of both series on the selected sheets.

title: Pressure-driven evolution of crystal and molecular structures reshapes excited-state competition in coronene
summary: Molecular nanocarbons exhibit unique optoelectronic properties and considered as promising candidates for organic device applications, however, understanding how molecular geometry and crystal packing jointly govern physical properties remains a fundamental challenge in π-conjugated molecular materials. Here, we demonstrate how these structural factors modulate the photoluminescence of coronene under high pressure. Combining high-pressure single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, optical spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations, we establish a relationship between distinct structural changes and the evolution of competing emissive states. Our results reveal that crystal polymorphism modifies the balance between free-exciton (FE) and self-trapped-exciton (STE) emission, while pressure-induced molecular bending is associated with a nonmonotonic evolution of STE emission. As intermolecular distances shorten, enhanced intermolecular electronic interactions give rise to excimer-related emission, introducing an additional emissive pathway. Although pressure-dependent optical properties of coronene have been linked to changes in crystal packing, our findings highlight that the optical response of a molecular solid is not governed by molecular deformation or crystal packing alone, but emerges from their interplay with intermolecular electronic coupling. By directly resolving molecular bending alongside changes in excited-state emission, this work provides insight into how distinct structural degrees of freedom can reshape the photophysical behavior of π-conjugated molecular solids.

title: Algebra-Valued Yang-Mills-Type Theories: Polynomial Obstructions and Holonomy Reductions
summary: We study algebra-valued Yang-Mills-type ($A$-YMT) theories on a smooth $n$-manifold $M$, where connections take values in an $\mathfrak{m}$-graded algebra $(A, *)$ and descend to an associated bundle $E_A = P \times_ρA \to M$. We derive the field equations, gauge transformations, and generalized Bianchi identities, showing that affine Ehresmann compatibility forces the vertical image of $\mathfrak{g}$ into the Lie nucleus $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{Lie}}(A)$ of $[x,y]_* = x*y - y*x$, and that gauge covariance and the Bianchi identity are obstructed precisely by the Jacobiator $\mathrm{Jac}_{[\cdot,\cdot]_*}$ (leaving principal $G$-gauge symmetries anomaly-free). We then prove obstructions in three settings. First, internal-product Chern-Weil and self-dual $A$-YMT functionals vanish in weak $(2,s)$-solvable algebras, invariant under $(Q,S)$-splitting extensions. Second, in reductive Cartan-Yang-Mills theories on $A = \mathbb{R}^k \oplus \mathfrak{h}$, quartic-block parenthesization yields a strict cutoff at $n \ge 8$, while binary-tree halving yields an exact Jacobsthal-number cutoff ($n - 4 \notin \bigcup_{r \ge 3}\{2 J_r, J_{r+1}\}$, plus rank vanishing for $n \ge k + 5$). We catalog Berger holonomy reductions for $4 \le n \le 7$, proving an on-shell vanishing (torsion-free) vs. off-shell survival (torsionful) dichotomy in 4D for $U(2)$ and $SU(2)$ connections---via $e \curlywedge_\rtimes (e \curlywedge_\rtimes Ω_ω) = \frac{1}{2}(e \curlywedge_\rtimes e) \curlywedge_\rtimes Ω_ω$---and in 7D for $G_2$-connections. Third, we prove an associator-quotient collapse and Jacobiator vertex dichotomy for odd-dimensional internal $A$-Chern-Simons theories, with applications to $A$-$BF$ theories, octonionic and reductive Higgs Proca mass spectra, and reductive dualities.

authors: Paulo Michel Longo Tavares da Silva
title: Dynamical Gauss--Bonnet Sum Rules and Global Consistency in Five-Dimensional Braneworld Cosmology
summary: We derive an exact dynamical consistency relation for a smooth, periodically compactified five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet cosmology sourced by a real, minimally coupled canonical scalar field. For a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaitre--Robertson--Walker slicing and a generally time-dependent warp factor, a contraction of the bulk equations eliminates both the scalar potential and the bulk cosmological constant. A direct orthonormal-curvature reconstruction gives the independent diagonal and mixed field equations and verifies the contracted Gauss--Bonnet identity. The integrated relation separates an exact total derivative from the dynamically active Lovelock sector. Importantly, satisfying the integrated sum rule alone does not imply a solution of the complete system. We prove that, for positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling, a smooth periodic time-independent warp factor and a canonical scalar exclude all exact expanding power-law scale factors $a(t)\propto t^p$ with $p>0$. This strengthens the previously established de Sitter sign obstruction and removes an earlier interpretation of $p=1/2$ as an admissible sign-compatible physical branch. For time-dependent warping, we reformulate bouncing conditions using proper time and the physical scale factor on each constant-$y$ hypersurface. We compare the common $w=-1$ geometric member with the perturbative weighted construction of Dias, Hoff da Silva, and da Rocha. At the level of the unexpanded Ricci-trace rearrangement, the curvature-only tensor contribution differs from the full Lanczos contraction by a definite scalar-curvature term. This distinction, and the additional independent field equations, delimit the physical conclusions that may be drawn from a necessary integrated condition.

title: Theoretical exploration of ambient-pressure superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate: A strategy of atomic substitution for tuning chemical pressure
summary: The possibility of ambient-pressure superconductivity in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$ is theoretically explored via chemical substitution. Using first-principles and many-body calculations, we propose substituting $\mathrm{Ba}$ at the lanthanide site to exert chemical pressure, thereby mitigating the octahedral distortions that suppress superconductivity. Phonon calculations demonstrate the dynamical stability of the high-symmetry tetragonal phase in $\mathrm{La_{3-\it{x}}Ba_{\it{x}}Ni_2O_7}$ at a small doping ratio of $x \sim 0.15$. By applying the fluctuation exchange approximation to an effective model Hamiltonian derived from this stable structure, we calculate the Eliashberg eigenvalue $λ$ to evaluate the relative superconducting transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ to existing unconventional superconductors. We conclude that $s_\pm$-wave superconductivity is likely to emerge, as the required $\mathrm{Ba}$ concentration ($x \sim 0.15$) is sufficiently small to minimize the detrimental suppression of superconductivity induced by hole doping.

title: Toward a Holographic Representation Theory of the Bosonic de Sitter Discrete Series
comment: 27 pages. Contribution to the proceedings of the 36th International Colloquium on Group Theoretical Methods in Physics (Group36), Valladolid, Spain, 2026

title: delta-Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Simple Lie Algebras with Values in Arbitrary Modules
summary: We determine the spaces of \(δ\)-derivations of finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras with values in arbitrary modules for \(δ\ne0,1\). In rank at least two, these derivations vanish unless \(δ=\frac{1}{2}\), in which case they are precisely the module homomorphisms from the adjoint module. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), we characterize the derivation spaces in terms of Casimir eigenspaces and determine when they are nonzero. When the coefficient module is simple, every nonzero derivation module is simple except possibly at \(δ=2\), where it has a simple essential socle with a finite-dimensional semisimple quotient. We describe these modules via translation functors and give explicit formulas for the derivations.

title: Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD$_3$
comment: 14 pages, 1 figure, 1 table; includes Supplemental Material
summary: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an $S_3$ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2^{(1)}$ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_3\times\mathrm{Spin}(8)_{-1}$ Chern-Simons-Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the $(\mathbf{8}_{\mathrm{adj}},\mathbf{8}_v)$ representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_{3/2}$ QCD$_3$ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's unitary symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. The continuum theories are proposed to recover lattice time reversal at criticality. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.

title: Baryon and lepton asymmetries across the cosmic QCD transition: effects of a 3D first-order surface
summary: We investigate the cosmological QCD phase transition by calculating the cosmic trajectories from the five equations that impose the conservation of the baryon and lepton asymmetries, the charge neutrality of the Universe, and $β$ equilibrium. We perform the calculation using for the first time the four-dimensional $(T, μ_B, μ_Q, μ_S)$ Constant Entropy Contour equation of state, which for $μ_S = 0$ ($β$-equilibrium) features a critical line and a first-order phase transition (FOPT) surface in the three-dimensional $(T, μ_B, μ_Q)$ space. We first show that, within the standard cosmological scenario with baryon asymmetry $b_{\text{obs}}=8.65\cdot 10^{-11}$, the lepton asymmetries alone can never induce a FOPT. We then explore the non-standard cosmological scenario with large values of $b$ and find that reaching a FOPT requires $b\gtrsim0.028$ during the QCD epoch. Such a value is compatible with observations only if the baryon asymmetry is diluted to $b_{\text{obs}}$ after the transition, which a period of little inflation would provide with $N\approx6.5$ $e$-folds of expansion. Finally, we study the phenomenological imprints on the equation of state and primordial black hole (PBH) formation, showing that pion condensation at large lepton asymmetries drives $c_s^2 > 1/3$ and shifts the PBH peak to sub-solar masses ($0.3-0.8\,M_\odot$), while the large-$b$ FOPT yields a narrow spike around $4.2\,M_\odot$.

title: Cubic local observability of Gaussian-blind sources in thermal $φ^4_2$ fields
summary: We study external sources that are invisible to a spatially local observation in a massive Gaussian thermal field on a circle. A quadratic-reference calibration removes the first-order thermal mass-shift signal. For the resulting quartic model we prove a cutoff-independent, source-uniform $C^1$ expansion of local Wick cubic means. Its leading operator has the time-integrated cube of the thermal covariance as its kernel. A positive bilateral Laplace representation proves injectivity on the entire external source space, while analyticity gives exponential singular-value upper bounds. The expansion yields local Araki relative-entropy lower bounds on every fixed finite-dimensional source space, and a uniform separation theorem at every prescribed Sobolev resolution. Under an additional interval-length condition, a reflection-positivity identity yields an explicit, nonoptimal double-logarithmic conditional stability bound for this specific thermal kernel. Continuum probability estimates and the integrability assumptions of the Feynman--Kac--Nelson construction are verified in Section~3.

title: Dopant-vacancy complexes as single-photon-emitter candidates in monolayer silicon carbide: radiative and nonradiative decay
summary: Solid-state color centers have emerged as promising single-photon sources (SPSs). In particular, color centers in two-dimensional (2D) materials combine high photon brightness with scalable fabrication and ease of integration, offering a versatile platform for quantum information technologies. Realizing high-efficiency SPSs, however, requires strong radiative emission and negligible nonradiative decay. Using first-principles calculations, we assess radiative and nonradiative decay in dopant-vacancy complexes XSiVC (X = N, O, P, and S) in monolayer silicon carbide. All four defects exhibit stable neutral charge states and inter-defect optical transitions. Among them, PSiVC emerges as the leading single-photon-emitter candidate, combining rapid radiative decay with negligible nonradiative decay and a near-unity quantum yield within the modeled channels. By contrast, multiphonon decay limits the quantum yield of NSiVC despite its high Debye-Waller factor. Hyperfine tensors provide characteristic signatures for identifying the spin-active centers. Beyond identifying promising candidates, these results establish a joint radiative-nonradiative screening strategy and provide theoretical guidance for the rational design of color centers as solid-state SPSs.

title: Full-shape analysis of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum and bispectrum: validation on simulations
summary: The Lyman-$α$ (LyA) forest of neutral hydrogen provides a large-volume, high-resolution map of cosmological fluctuations from optical spectra at high redshift. To extract more information from the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we derive an effective field theory (EFT) model for joint full-shape analyses of the LyA forest data. It combines the one-loop power spectrum of the LyA forest (FF), and of its cross-correlation with dark-matter halos, used as proxies for high-redshift quasars (FQ), with the tree-level bispectrum of the LyA forest (FFF). Importantly, the bispectrum breaks the LyA-specific degeneracy between the mean flux and the amplitude of the power spectrum. We validate our theory framework on idealized large-volume LyA forest mocks painted onto the AbacusSummit N-body simulation suite at redshift z=2.5. Fitting scales up to $k_\mathrm{max}^{FF\,(FQ)}=0.6\,(0.3)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k_\mathrm{max}^{FFF}=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum, our full-shape analysis yields unbiased constraints on the cosmological parameters in simulations. For a fully sampled flux field in a simulated volume of $V=8\,h^{-3}\,{\rm Gpc}^3$, we measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$, to $0.6\%$, the matter density, $Ω_{\rm m}$, to $1.6\%$ and the amplitude of matter clustering, $σ_8$, to $3.5\%$. Adding the bispectrum improves the constraints on $σ_8$ by $28\%$. We also demonstrate that the inclusion of the quasar one-loop power spectrum (QQ) and tree-level bispectrum (QQQ) further improves cosmological constraints by $\approx 35\%$ using $k_\mathrm{max}^{QQ,\,(QQQ)}=0.2,\,(0.08)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Our theory framework enables full-shape analyses of high-redshift data from DESI and its successor DESI-II, enhancing knowledge of the growth of structure of the Universe during matter-domination.

title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
summary: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$.
